slides.title: What is a Variable?
slides.content: A variable is a named container that stores data in memory. Think of it as a labeled box that holds a value you can use and change later.

slides.title: Declaring Variables
slides.content: Declare a variable by specifying its type, then a name, and optionally assigning a value. The syntax is: type variableName = value;

exercise.prompt: Choose the correct keyword to declare an integer.

slides.title: Common Data Types
slides.content: C# has several built-in types. int stores whole numbers, double stores decimals, bool stores true or false, string stores text, and char stores a single character.

slides.title: Naming Conventions
slides.content: Use camelCase for local variables: first word lowercase, subsequent words capitalized. Use PascalCase for methods and classes. Names should be descriptive.

slides.title: The var Keyword
slides.content: The var keyword lets the compiler infer the type from the assigned value. The variable is still strongly typed—you just don't write the type explicitly.

slides.title: Constants with const
slides.content: Use const to declare a variable whose value cannot change. Constants must be initialized at declaration and are typically named in PascalCase.

exercise.prompt: Declare a const double called Pi with value 3.14 and print it.
hints: Make sure your code includes the required keywords/elements: class, static
When run, your code should output: 3.14

slides.title: String Interpolation
slides.content: String interpolation lets you embed variables directly inside a string using $"...". Place the variable name in curly braces to insert its value.

slides.title: Type Conversion
slides.content: Convert between types using Parse(), ToString(), or Convert.ToXxx(). Be careful—invalid conversions throw exceptions, so validate input when needed.

slides.title: Flow Builder: Variables
slides.content: Use the Flow Builder to declare an int and a string, then output them.

exercise.prompt: Build a flow that declares int age = 25 and string name = 'Alice', then outputs name
